_comment: Stage-2 ASC sweep. 37 runs. Derived from the 24 completed stage-1 runs.
Stage 1 hit the grid boundary in all three dimensions: the best run was
pt -0.6 / walk -0.41 / bike -1.51 (share_mae 1.49pp), with monotone
improvement toward less-negative pt and more-negative walk/bike. The signed
errors (mvv) of that run and their ln(target/sim) ASC updates were:
car           +0.46pp  -> -0.013  (reference, stays 0: already on target)
car_passenger +0.09pp  -> -0.007  (stays -2.31: already on target)
PT is the dominant error and needs to move UP (less negative), which lands
almost exactly on the OLD calibrated -0.36 - i.e. PT needed essentially no
dU_car compensation, unlike what stage 1 assumed.
Ranges extend from the stage-1 best in the direction each update points.
walk/bike are kept near the stage-1 best rather than fully shifted, because
raising PT pulls ~3.5pp out of the other modes and will reduce the walk/bike
surplus on its own - applying all updates at full size would double-correct.
'formula_update' is the exact simultaneous-update point, as a direct test.
NOTE the zonal split in PT, which no single global ASC can fix: umland PT is
6.4% vs 11% target (update +0.54) while munich PT is 22.7% vs 24% (+0.06).
Expect leftover PT error in the umland; that points at PT level-of-service
there, not at the ASC.
